claims: Marion County, Florida was created on March 14, 1844.
Marion County, Florida is named for Revolutionary War General Francis Marion.
Marion County, Florida is a North Central Florida region.
Marion County, Florida holds 35% of Florida's horses.
Marion County, Florida has 46% of Florida's thoroughbreds.
The county seat of Marion County, Florida is Ocala.
Major cities and areas in Marion County, Florida include Ocala, The Villages, Belleview, Dunnellon, Reddick, and McIntosh.
As of the 2020 census, the population of Marion County, Florida was 375,908.
2020-2024 data shows a median household income of roughly $61,010 in Marion County, Florida.
Attractions in Marion County, Florida include Silver Springs State Park, Rainbow Springs, Ocala National Forest, and historical sites in downtown Ocala.
The Marion County Sheriff’s Office manages local law enforcement in Marion County, Florida, including inmate searches and community watch programs.
There are 17 Marion Counties in the United States
